title: EyeNet Invest
text:
Edge Vision · Operational Action · Seed Ladder 
   EyeNet investor primer 
   On-premises vision that detects, decides, and acts — for homes, care, offices, ships, industrial sites, and venues where cloud cameras cannot follow. 
     Type  Investor Primer    Date  21 October 2026    Structure  Bet · Wedges · Motions · Seed · Footprint    Seed ladder  $0.5M → $1M → $2.5M   
 
 On-premises vision that detects, decides, and acts — distilled from the value thesis and business plan for investor discussion. 
   01  The bet  Incumbents sell cloud storage; EyeNet sells sovereignty and operational action.    02  What changes  Edge, action, and hardware-bound scale — not another camera cloud.    03  Where it pays  Highest-value wedges across care, HR, signage, family, security, and shipping.    04  How it is sold  B2C Light, B2B, and Enterprise motions with cite-backed pockets.    05  Seed ladder  $0.5M → $1M → $2.5M ladder with staged outcomes.    06  Footprint  What each seed step funds: product, GTM, and footprint.    07  Project status  Readiness, partners, and growth path.    08  Market sources  Public URLs behind commercial addressable-pocket counts.

title: The bet
text:
01  The bet  
 Incumbents sell cloud storage, bandwidth, and recordings. EyeNet sells sovereignty and operational action: any camera becomes a vision node on a ~16 GB PC, first detection in minutes, no per-camera licenses, and video that never has to leave the site. Scale is hardware-bound — one room to a campus — with no technical ceiling. 

       
         
           $0.5–1.5B 
           B2C TAM, U.S. 
           Conservative consumer addressable market. 
         
         
           $2–4B 
           B2B / Enterprise TAM 
           U.S. mid-market and strategic accounts. 
         
         
           1–3% 
           B2C Share → $5–45M 
           Plan target share of B2C TAM. 
         
         
           1–2% 
           Enterprise → $20–80M 
           Plan target share of enterprise TAM.

title: What changes
text:
02  What changes  
 Users are not locked to a camera wall. The platform watches 24/7; the right person gets a targeted alert — mobile, email, webhook, clinical app, or HubSpot — only when something needs them. Ordinary cameras become an always-on assistant that decides and acts on premises, including when the internet is down. 

       
         
           Edge 
           Not cloud-bound 
           On-device AI. Full offline. Data sovereignty by default. Processing and storage stay on premises. 
         
         
           Action 
           Not passive VMS 
           Triggers fire mobile, email, webhooks, signage, and gates. Each camera has its own rules. 
         
         
           Scale 
           Hardware-bound 
           Any IP, WiFi, or phone camera. ~16 GB PC. One room to an enterprise mesh. No GPU farm. 
         
       

       
         
           Incumbents sell 
           
             Cloud storage & monthly bandwidth 
             Passive recordings & dashboards 
             Generic “AI boxes” 
             Projects that take quarters 
           
         
         
           EyeNet ships 
           
             On-prem decisions & zero video cloud 
             Targeted notifications that run the operation 
             Purpose-built apps for real jobs 
             Detection in minutes — scale by hardware 
           
         
       

       How it multiplies operator capacity 
       
          Vision nodes  — face, count, demographics, and routes on cameras the site already owns. 
          Entrances, restricted zones, VIP watchlists  — headcount, unauthorised presence, and person-of-interest alerts without extra posts. 
          Signage that reads the room  — age, gender, and group size switch content in milliseconds, with impressions and dwell. 
          Remote control from a phone  — VPN access to cameras, triggers, and dashboards. Footage stays on premises even when the operator does not.

title: Where it pays
text:
03  Where it pays  
 Six wedges. Same platform. The market others abandon is connectivity- and privacy-hostile: ships, industrial sites, clinics, family homes, night posts, Virtual Wards. 

       
         
           
             Wedge 
             Buyer 
             Why it is paid for 
           
         
         
           
              HR presence  
             HR, facilities, office ops 
             Automatic staff presence on-site and remote, with zero manual roll-call. HubSpot is the first CRM connector. 
           
           
              Vision-adaptive intelligent signage  
             Retail, venues, agencies, brand studios 
             Age, gender, and group size switch playlists in milliseconds. Impressions, dwell, and A/B turn screens into a measurable studio. 
           
           
              Family protection at home and remote  
             Families, parents, students living away 
             Intrusion, unknown-person, and presence alerts for the home and for people living away. Footage stays local. 
           
           
              Home care / Virtual Ward  
             Care provider, clinician, Talos / TMAIX 
             Caregiver presence, fall, help-call, and zone events into the health stack — tokenized, not cloud video. Safety layer vitals-only RPM cannot fake. 
           
           
              Security: night and perimeter  
             Security firms, corporate & industrial sites 
             Guard vigilance, perimeter Presence, Vradar motion, and forensics. Night coverage stops scaling 1:1 with sites. 
           
           
              Shipping and industrial  
             Captain, fleet manager, plant & site ops 
             Who is onboard or on site, restricted zones, and headcount packs. Full local ops; sync on thin links. Matrix when offline.

title: Seed scenarios — from burn up
text:
05  Seed scenarios — from burn up  
 The seed burn floor is $500K — enough for about one year of product, launch, and working capital. Checks of $1M and $2.5M sit above that floor. Extra capital does not rewrite unit economics. It buys speed: more pilots, faster sales coverage, and an earlier geographic footprint. 

       
         
           $500K 
           Burn Floor · Year-1 Ops 
           Personnel, marketing/CAC, tech, ops — lean runway. 
         
         
           $1M 
           Base Seed 
           Burn covered, plus headroom for a fuller GTM. 
         
         
           $2.5M 
           Accelerate Seed 
           Same economics, earlier scale and footprint. 
         
       

       
         
           
             Scenario 
             Seed in 
             What it buys 
             Typical next round 
           
         
         
           
              Burn floor  
             $500K 
             Personnel ~$180K, marketing/CAC ~$135K, tech ~$125K, ops/R&D ~$60K. Launch, first pilots, lean runway. 
             Series A / growth ~$700K–$1M after traction 
           
           
              Base  
             $1M 
             Burn covered, plus fuller GTM. Plan terms: ~25% at $3M pre ($4M post). Target: 5–10 pilots, $50–100K ARR, 50-lead pipeline, 2–3 partners. 
             Series A $2–3M on $8–12M pre (Q3–Q4 2026) 
           
           
              Accelerate  
             $2.5M 
             Same core economics, earlier scale: denser sales, marketing, and multi-site footprint in the seed window. Dilution set by negotiated pre-money. 
             Series A still available for land-and-expand; larger seed compresses time to that raise 
           
         
       

       
         Instrument 
         Convertible note or SAFE across scenarios. The $1M and $2.5M figures both appear in the business-plan set; treat them as capital choices on the same ladder, not as competing truths.

title: Footprint steps by scenario
text:
06  Footprint steps by scenario  
 Organizational build-out scales with capital above burn. Unit economics stay the same; the company simply stands up earlier. 

       
         
           
             Step 
             Burn $500K 
             Base $1M 
             Accelerate $2.5M 
           
         
         
           
              1 · Greek unit  
             Yes — EU pilot, GDPR-first, lean team 
             Yes — formal Greek business unit 
             Yes — Greek unit as EU operating base 
           
           
              2 · U.S. business unit  
             Lean commercial start in primary market 
             Yes — U.S. unit for enterprise + B2C launch 
             Yes — U.S. unit with denser sales and partner coverage 
           
           
              3 · London office  
             — 
             — 
             Yes — London representation for UK / North-West Europe 
           
         
       

       Greece is the plan’s EU pilot (compliance, education, tourism). The United States is the primary commercial market. London appears only on the high seed: a representation office, not a second R&D center. 

       
         
           What is hard to copy 
           Privacy-first edge computer vision, six vertical cases on one platform — HR, signage, family protection, home care, night and perimeter security, shipping and industrial — plus partner channels: Talos / TMAIX in eHealth, maritime and plant ops, HubSpot-first CRM. Presence, Vradar, Sentinel, and Matrix are one fabric. A feature checkbox does not reproduce that stack. 
         
         
           What to underwrite 
           Burn floor first, then how much speed to buy. CAC, LTV, and payback are the core. Capital above $500K accelerates the same motions — consumer volume, mid-market land-and-expand, enterprise ACV — and the footprint steps above. 
         
       

       EyeNet Vision · Investor primer · Confidential for investor discussion. title: Addendum A — Project status
text:
07  Addendum A — Project status  
 Product readiness and partners from the July 2026 business-plan primer, plus the capital and growth path restated in the same seed-ladder language as sections 05–06. Team started July 2024; working prototype in under six months. Five of six products are beta-ready. 

       The six products 
       
         
           
             Product 
             Job 
           
         
         
           
              EyeNet Presence  
             Automatic attendance with face + QR/NFC check-in. Replaces paper timesheets and badge swipes. 
           
           
              EyeNet Signage  
             Digital screens that change content based on who is watching (age, gender). Measurable advertising. 
           
           
              EyeNet Vradar  
             Alert brain: rules such as crowd thresholds that fire mobile, email, or other actions. Powers the rest of the stack. 
           
           
              EyeNet Gate  
             Entrance and exit monitoring. Counts people in and out; flags suspicious faces in real time. 
           
           
              EyeNet Sentinel  
             Wearable camera glasses + drones for VIP / bodyguard teams. Spots persons of interest in a crowd. 
           
           
              EyeNet Matrix  
             One dashboard across dozens of sites. Franchise chains, shipping fleets, multi-location businesses. 
           
         
       
       Status: five of six products beta-ready and with design partners for real-world testing (Q3 2026). 

       Current milestones 
       
          July 2024:  Working prototype delivered in under six months. 
          Q3 2026:  Five of six products beta-ready and in the hands of design partners. 
          Two distribution partners signed:  TMA (EyeNet-branded) and NewGen Group (white-label). Both early-stage, pursuing hot leads across municipalities, enterprises, and maritime clients. 
          Deloitte engagement:  NewGen has laid groundwork for a demo with Deloitte Greece; presentation to the Deloitte EMEA Cyber Security Committee tentatively scheduled for September 2026. 
          LG International hot lead:  TMA is positioning EyeNet for a European municipality and has identified a high-potential early-stage lead with LG International — major upside if it converts. 
       

       Capital and growth path 
       Same seed ladder as section 05: burn floor first, then how much speed to buy. Extra capital does not rewrite unit economics — it buys earlier pilots, denser sales, and the footprint steps in section 06. Instrument: convertible note or SAFE across scenarios. 

       
         
           
             Horizon 
             Plan 
           
         
         
           
              Seed · Burn floor · $500K  
             Year-1 ops floor: launch, first pilots, lean runway. Personnel / marketing / tech / ops covered; Greek unit as EU pilot. Typical next: Series A / growth ~$700K–$1M after traction. 
           
           
              Seed · Base · $1M  
             Burn covered, plus fuller GTM. Plan terms: ~25% at $3M pre ($4M post). Target: 5–10 pilots, $50–100K ARR, 50-lead pipeline, 2–3 partners; formal Greek + U.S. units. Typical next: Series A $2–3M on $8–12M pre (Q3–Q4 2026). 
           
           
              Seed · Accelerate · $2.5M  
             Same core economics, earlier scale: denser sales and multi-site footprint in the seed window; Greek + U.S. units and London representation. Series A still available for land-and-expand; larger seed compresses time to that raise. 
           
           
              Series A  
             Size and timing scale with seed choice: ~$700K–$1M after burn-floor traction; $2–3M on the base path; larger seed still leaves Series A for land-and-expand. Use of proceeds: dedicated sales, marketing ramp, path toward ~200 customers. 
           
           
              2027  
             ~$1M revenue · 50 B2B · ~600 consumer users — first commercial proof after seed launch of the five beta-ready products. 
           
           
              2028  
             ~$8M revenue · 200 B2B · 6,000+ consumer — breakeven. Capital above burn accelerates arrival; unit economics stay the same. 
           
           
              2029  
             ~$26M revenue · 500 B2B · 20,000+ consumer — solidly profitable on the three motions (B2C Light, B2B Starter / Pro, Enterprise). 
           
           
              2030–2031  
             Exit path: IPO or strategic acquisition at $500M–$1B (plan target range). 
           
         
       

       Why this path is underwritable 
       
          Products are built, not imagined:  Five of six apps exist as working beta. Capital on the seed ladder buys selling what works — computer vision, recognition, and alert automation are already done — not building from scratch. 
          Distribution is already on board:  TMA and NewGen are signed partners pursuing leads, not letters of intent. That de-risks the first ~50 paying customers and the base-seed pipeline target. 
          Deloitte is a force multiplier in waiting:  EMEA Cyber Security Committee presentation tentatively on the calendar for September 2026. 
          LG International is a global-scale multiplier:  Early-stage hot lead, not a closed deal. A win with LG’s trading and investment arm can unlock manufacturing, logistics, retail, and government supply-chain distribution and open other Korean / Asian conglomerate doors. 
          Burn floor first, then speed:  Underwrite $500K ops, then choose $1M or $2.5M for how fast footprint and GTM stand up. CAC, LTV, and payback in How it is sold hold across all three seed scenarios. 
       
       Seed scenarios and footprint detail: sections 05–06. TAM share, CAC / LTV, and package pricing: How it is sold and Addendum B. Growth years and exit ranges from eyenet-web/bp/onepager/primer.html (July 2026), restated on the seed ladder.
